Filled circles, uppercase only

Same idea as the circled alphabet with the colours swapped: the disc is filled and the letter is cut out of it, so a line of this reads as a row of badges rather than as writing. Each letter is its own character in the Enclosed Alphanumeric Supplement, starting at U+1F150, and there is a limitation built into the block. Only capitals were ever encoded. No lowercase negative circled set exists, so lowercase input comes back as the same filled capitals.

The digits come from somewhere else entirely, the dingbat negative-circled numbers running from ⓿ through ❾, which is why they often render on devices where the letters do not. Letter coverage is thinner than for plain circled, these being much newer additions to the standard, and a device without them shows rectangles. Short and prominent is the use: a rank in a leaderboard post, a tag at the front of a line, three or four characters at most.

Also searched as: black bubble text generator, filled circle letters, negative circled text copy paste.

Where Negative Circled text works, and where it does not

WorksVery widely supported — these are long-standing characters and most fonts on most devices have them. Watch outSome Android system fonts miss the lowercase enclosed letters and draw an empty box instead.

Negative Circled questions

Why does lowercase come out looking like uppercase?

There is no lowercase version to give you. Unicode encoded a set of negative circled capitals and never added the matching lowercase, unlike the plain circled block which has both. Rather than drop your lowercase letters or leave them unstyled in the middle of a badge, this site maps them to the same filled capitals.

Where do the filled digits come from?

Not from the same block as the letters. They are dingbat characters, ⓿ and ❶ through ❾, which have been in Unicode far longer and appear in many more fonts. That mismatch in age is why a filled number often shows correctly on a device that draws empty rectangles for the filled letters beside it.

Does it work on Instagram?

Bios and comments take the characters like any other text, but this block is newer and less widely covered than plain bubble letters, so some readers will see rectangles where you see discs. Keep it to two or three characters, put nothing essential inside them, and use plain circled if you want safer coverage.
